questions.stem: He is superior ___ me in rank.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives — superior, inferior, senior, junior — take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.stem: She was absorbed ___ her work.
questions.explanation: 'Absorbed in' means deeply engrossed in something.

questions.stem: He complied ___ my request.
questions.explanation: 'Comply with' a request or rule is the fixed pattern.

questions.stem: He is entitled ___ a pension.
questions.explanation: 'Entitled to' something means having a right to it.

questions.stem: Students have no access ___ these files.
questions.explanation: 'Access to' is the fixed collocation.

questions.stem: He is capable ___ doing the job.
questions.explanation: 'Capable of' takes a gerund.

questions.stem: I am aware ___ the situation.
questions.explanation: 'Aware of' is the standard form.

questions.stem: He is devoted ___ his duty.
questions.explanation: 'Devoted to' means dedicated to.

questions.stem: She is proud ___ her son.
questions.explanation: 'Proud of' is the fixed collocation.

questions.stem: He is suffering ___ fever.
questions.explanation: 'Suffer from' an illness is the fixed pattern.

questions.stem: They are engaged ___ business.
questions.explanation: 'Engaged in' an activity; 'engaged to' a person one will marry.

questions.stem: We ___ for two hours when he finally arrived.
questions.explanation: An action continuing up to a point in the past takes the past perfect continuous.

questions.stem: If you had come earlier, you ___ him.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: 'had + past participle' pairs with 'would have + past participle'.

questions.stem: He said he ___ the work by evening.
questions.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' after a past reporting verb.

questions.stem: I ___ him for ten years.
questions.explanation: A state continuing to the present takes the present perfect; 'know' is not used in continuous form.

questions.stem: She ___ in Khulna before moving to Dhaka.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past events takes the past perfect.

questions.stem: He will call me as soon as he ___ .
questions.explanation: After 'as soon as', a future action is expressed by the simple present.

questions.stem: I have never ___ such a beautiful scene.
questions.explanation: The present perfect takes the past participle 'seen'.

questions.stem: She ___ when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by another takes the past continuous.

questions.stem: He ___ not come yet.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' with an action not completed takes the present perfect: has not come.

questions.stem: The sun ___ in the west.
questions.explanation: A universal truth takes the simple present.

questions.stem: They ___ the bridge last year.
questions.explanation: 'Last year' is a definite past time, so the simple past is used.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Who taught you English?'
options: By whom you were taught English?
By whom were you taught English?
Who were you taught English by?
questions.explanation: In a passive question the auxiliary precedes the subject: By whom WERE you taught?

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Let him do it.'
options: Let it be done by him.
He is let to do it.
questions.explanation: 'Let + object + verb' becomes 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'The news surprised me.'
options: I was surprised by the news.
I was surprised at the news.
I am surprised of the news.
The news was surprised to me.
questions.explanation: Verbs of emotion such as surprise, shock and please take 'at' rather than 'by'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'They had finished the work.'
options: The work was finished by them.
The work has been finished by them.
The work had been finished by them.
The work is finished by them.
questions.explanation: Past perfect active becomes 'had been + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Keep the room clean.'
options: Let the room be kept clean.
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'The police arrested the thief.'
options: The thief is arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.
The thief has arrested by the police.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'He is writing a novel.'
options: A novel is written by him.
A novel is being written by him.
A novel was being written by him.
A novel has been written by him.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active becomes 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'They called him a fool.'
options: He is called a fool by them.
questions.explanation: With a factitive object the complement stays after the passive verb.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'You should do your duty.'
options: Your duty should do by you.
Your duty should be done by you.
Your duty is done by you.
Your duty was done by you.
questions.explanation: A modal becomes 'modal + be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'I shall complete the task.'
options: The task shall complete by me.
The task will be completed by me.
The task is completed by me.
The task was completed by me.
questions.explanation: Simple future active becomes 'will be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into active: 'The letter was posted by him.'
questions.explanation: 'Was + past participle' corresponds to the simple past active.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: Mother said, "May God bless you."
options: Mother said that God might bless me.
Mother prayed that God might bless me.
Mother told that God would bless me.
Mother wished God to bless me.
questions.explanation: An optative sentence takes a reporting verb of praying or wishing.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Who is there?"
questions.explanation: A wh-question is reported with statement order and a back-shifted verb.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I shall have finished by then."
options: He said that he will have finished by then.
He said that he would have finished by then.
He said that he had finished by then.
He said that he has finished by then.
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'shall have finished' becomes 'would have finished'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Will you help me?"
options: She asked me if I will help her.
She asked me if I would help her.
She said me whether I would help her.
She asked me would I help her.
questions.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would', and the question is reported with 'if'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am going to Dhaka tomorrow."
options: He said that he is going to Dhaka tomorrow.
He said that he was going to Dhaka the next day.
He said that he went to Dhaka the next day.
He said that he would go to Dhaka tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous, and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Do not make noise."
options: The teacher told us not to make noise.
The teacher said not to make noise.
The teacher asked that we do not make noise.
The teacher ordered us do not make noise.
questions.explanation: A negative imperative becomes 'told … not to + verb'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Where are you going?"
options: She asked me where was I going.
She asked me where I was going.
She said me where I am going.
She asked me where am I going.
questions.explanation: A reported wh-question drops the inversion.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I did it myself."
options: He said that he did it himself.
He said that he had done it himself.
He said that he has done it himself.
He said that he does it himself.
questions.explanation: The simple past shifts to the past perfect in reported speech.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "How are you?"
options: He asked me how was I.
He asked me how I was.
He said me how I am.
He asked me how am I.
questions.explanation: The reported question keeps statement order and back-shifts the verb.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said, "It is raining."
options: She said that it is raining.
She said that it was raining.
She says that it was raining.
She told that it is raining.
questions.explanation: The present continuous shifts to the past continuous.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I like tea."
options: He said that he likes tea.
He said that he liked tea.
He says that he liked tea.
He told that he likes tea.
questions.explanation: The simple present shifts to the simple past after a past reporting verb.

questions.stem: ‘সে এত দুর্বল যে হাঁটতে পারে না’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: He is so weak that he cannot walk.
He is very weak to walk.
He is such weak that he cannot walk.
He is so weak so he cannot walk.
questions.explanation: ‘এত … যে’ গঠনের ইংরেজি রূপ 'so … that'।

questions.stem: ‘সে অসুস্থ বলে আসেনি’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: He did not come because he was ill.
He did not come but he was ill.
He was ill so he came.
Because he did not come he was ill.
questions.explanation: কারণ বোঝাতে 'because' দিয়ে অধীন খণ্ডবাক্য যুক্ত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘যদি তুমি পরিশ্রম কর, তবে সফল হবে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: If you will work hard, you will succeed.
If you work hard, you will succeed.
If you worked hard, you will succeed.
If you work hard, you succeed.
questions.explanation: First conditional-এ if-clause-এ simple present ও main clause-এ 'will' বসে।

questions.stem: ‘আকাশে অনেক তারা আছে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: Many stars are in the sky.
There are many stars in the sky.
In the sky many stars have.
questions.explanation: অস্তিত্ব বোঝাতে 'There is / There are' গঠন ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘সে বই পড়তে ভালোবাসে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: 'Love' এর পরে gerund বা to-infinitive বসে; এখানে 'reading' শুদ্ধ।

questions.stem: ‘তুমি কি আমাকে সাহায্য করবে?’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: ভবিষ্যতের অনুরোধ বা প্রশ্নে দ্বিতীয় পুরুষে 'Will you' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘আমি তাকে চিনি না’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: 'Know' stative verb, তাই continuous রূপে বসে না।

questions.stem: ‘আমার ভাই একজন ডাক্তার’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: একবচন গণনাযোগ্য পেশার আগে 'a' বসে।

questions.stem: ‘আমি বাংলাদেশে বাস করি’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: স্থায়ী অবস্থা বোঝাতে simple present ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘তার বয়স দশ বছর’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: ইংরেজিতে বয়স প্রকাশের প্রচলিত গঠন 'He is ten years old'।

questions.stem: ‘সে একজন ভালো ছাত্র’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: একবচন গণনাযোগ্য বিশেষ্যের আগে 'a' বসে।

questions.stem: 'An apple of discord' means —
questions.explanation: From Greek myth — it means something that causes dispute.

questions.stem: 'To build castles in the air' means —
questions.explanation: It means to make plans that have no chance of being realised.

questions.stem: 'To go to the dogs' means —
questions.explanation: It means to deteriorate badly or be ruined.

questions.stem: 'A storm in a teacup' means —
questions.explanation: It describes great excitement about something trivial.

questions.stem: 'To read between the lines' means —
options: To read carefully word by word
questions.explanation: It means to understand what is implied rather than stated.

questions.stem: 'To add fuel to the fire' means —
questions.explanation: It means to worsen an already bad situation.

questions.stem: 'To face the music' means —
questions.explanation: It means to accept the unpleasant results of one's actions.

questions.stem: 'To break the ice' means —
questions.explanation: It means to ease initial awkwardness and begin talking.

questions.stem: 'In a nutshell' means —
questions.explanation: 'In a nutshell' means very concisely.

questions.stem: 'To pull one's leg' means —
questions.explanation: It means to joke with or tease someone.

questions.stem: 'At a loss' means —
questions.explanation: 'At a loss' means unable to decide what to do or say.

questions.stem: It is no use ___ over spilt milk.
questions.explanation: 'It is no use' is followed by a gerund.

questions.stem: He cannot help ___ at the joke.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot help' meaning 'cannot refrain from' takes a gerund.

questions.stem: He had better ___ at once.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' takes the bare infinitive.

questions.stem: I would rather you ___ now.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather + subject' takes the past tense for a present preference.

questions.stem: Would you mind ___ the window?
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind' is followed by a gerund.

questions.stem: She promised ___ me with the work.
questions.explanation: 'Promise' is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: They kept ___ for hours.
questions.explanation: 'Keep' meaning 'continue' takes a gerund.

questions.stem: He seems ___ tired today.
questions.explanation: 'Seem' is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: I saw him ___ the road.
questions.explanation: After a verb of perception a gerund-participle shows the action in progress.

questions.stem: He ___ to the office every day.
questions.explanation: A third-person singular subject takes the -s form.

questions.stem: The children are ___ in the garden.
questions.explanation: The present continuous takes the -ing form.

questions.stem: In 'The wise are respected everywhere', the word 'wise' is used as a —
questions.explanation: 'The + adjective' naming a class of people functions as a noun.

questions.stem: In 'Reading is a good habit', the word 'reading' is a —
questions.explanation: An -ing verb form used as the subject of a sentence is a gerund.

questions.stem: In 'Iron is a useful metal', the word 'iron' is a —
questions.explanation: A noun naming a substance is a material noun.

questions.stem: In 'A flock of birds flew away', the word 'flock' is a —
questions.explanation: A word naming a group taken as one unit is a collective noun.

questions.stem: In 'Bravery is a great virtue', the word 'bravery' is a —
questions.explanation: A quality that cannot be perceived by the senses is an abstract noun.

questions.stem: In 'This pen is mine', the word 'mine' is a —
questions.explanation: 'Mine' stands alone in place of a noun, so it is a possessive pronoun.

questions.stem: In 'He ran across the field', the word 'across' is a —
questions.explanation: It relates 'ran' to 'the field', so it is a preposition.

questions.stem: In 'He speaks English fluently', the word 'fluently' is a —
questions.explanation: It modifies the verb 'speaks', so it is an adverb of manner.

questions.stem: In 'Neither of them came', the word 'neither' is a —
questions.explanation: Here 'neither' stands in place of a noun, so it is a pronoun.

questions.stem: In 'She is very intelligent', the word 'intelligent' is a —
questions.explanation: It describes the subject, so it is an adjective.

questions.stem: In 'He walks slowly', the word 'slowly' is a —
questions.explanation: It tells how he walks, so it is an adverb of manner.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He returned to back home yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Return' already means 'come back', so 'returned back' is redundant.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: Let us discuss about the matter.
Let us discuss on the matter.
Let us discuss for the matter.
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb and takes no preposition.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: The cattle is grazing in the field.
The cattle are grazing in the field.
The cattles are grazing in the field.
The cattle was grazing in the field.
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' is a plural noun and takes a plural verb.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Perseverance' ends in -ance.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Bureaucracy' comes from 'bureau' and keeps the -eau spelling.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Millennium' has a double l and a double n.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is one of my best friend.
He is one of my best friends.
He is one of my best of friends.
He is one from my best friend.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Restaurant' ends in -aurant.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Vacuum' has one c and a double u.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Government' keeps the 'n' of 'govern'.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ful always has a single l.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'ameliorate'.
questions.explanation: 'Ameliorate' means to make something better.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'.
questions.explanation: 'Ubiquitous' means found everywhere at the same time.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'verbose'.
questions.explanation: 'Verbose' means using more words than needed.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'affluent'.
questions.explanation: 'Affluent' means rich; 'indigent' means poor.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'zenith'.
questions.explanation: 'Zenith' is the highest point; 'nadir' is the lowest.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'obsolete'.
questions.explanation: 'Obsolete' means no longer in use, outdated.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'prudent'.
questions.explanation: 'Prudent' means showing care and good judgement.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'compulsory'.
questions.explanation: 'Compulsory' means required; 'optional' means a matter of choice.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'brittle'.
questions.explanation: 'Brittle' breaks easily; 'flexible' bends without breaking.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'brave'.
questions.explanation: 'Brave' and 'courageous' are synonyms.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'ancient' in the sense of people.
questions.explanation: Applied to people, the contrast with 'ancient' or aged is 'youthful'.
